subject: how to construct a beta-bernoulli model correctly?

messages.author: ac2d8451d16a0688
messages.subject: how to construct a beta-bernoulli model correctly?
parts:
Hi,

I use rstan to construct a beta-bernoulli model. The model can run, but the result of parameter estimation and lp__ seem not right, I have no 

idea what is the problem of my code. 

In my experiment, there are 200 trials. In each trial, participants choose one of two options depending on the probability (theta in code). The 

theta of each trial follows a beta distribution with two parameters, a and b. The theta and its parameters would update after participants

receive new information (x and n in code). I would like to estimate the parameter a and b. My code is as follows, any help would be appreciated!

data{
int<lower=0> J;   // trial number
int<lower=0> y[J]; // response
real x[J];  // information
int n[J]; // 
}

parameters{
real<lower=0,upper=1> theta[J]; 
real<lower=0> a;
real<lower=0> b;
}

transformed parameters{
real<lower=0> aa[J];
real<lower=0> bb[J];
for (i in 1:J) {
aa[i] <- x[i]+a;
bb[i]<- n[i]-x[i]+b;
}
}

model{
for (i in 1:J)
theta[i]~beta(aa[i],bb[i]);
for (j in 1:J)
y[j]~bernoulli(theta[j]);
}

> Hi,
>
> I use rstan to construct a beta-bernoulli model. The model can run, but the result of parameter estimation and lp__ seem not right, I have no
>
> idea what is the problem of my code.

Not right in what way? Stan drops constant additive
terms, so lp__ isn't going to report the full joint log
probability.

Have you tried simulating data according to the model and
fitting it to see if you recover the right values?

You also have improper priors on a and b, which even if it
doesn't cause an improper posterior in theory, may allow
a and b to wander up to very large values (this is common
in these kinds of models --- there's an illustration in
Bayesian Data Analysis in the intro to hierarchical models).

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] how to construct a beta-bernoulli model correctly?
parts:
I should've also added that if you use

increment_log_prob(foo_log(y,...));

instead of

y ~ foo(...);

then you will get all of the terms, even as of Stan 2.2.

We should prioritize all these little feature requests. We're
doing a better job of hitting bigger ones.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] how to construct a beta-bernoulli model correctly?
parts:
I'm not the applied statistician on the team, but I
wonder if the beta-bernoulli even makes sense. The
beta-binomial is an overdispersed form of the binomial,
but I don't see what a beta-bernoulli gives you.
Thus I suspect your posterior isn't properly identified
with only the improper priors on a and b.

What do the traceplots look like and what values are you
getting for a and b? Does Stan think it's converged?

There's a chapter in the manual on problematic posteriors,
including improper posteriors.

- Bob
